title: DIC Entitlement for Surviving Spouses: Qualifying Death and Qualifying Marriage
content:
Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) for a surviving spouse rests on two separate conditions: one about the veteran's death and one about the spouse's marriage to the veteran.

## 1. The veteran's death

DIC is payable to a surviving spouse when the veteran:

- (a) died in service; or
- (b) died of a service-connected disability; or
- (c) was rated totally disabled for the total-disability period before death; or was rated totally disabled continuously from discharge for the total-disability period from discharge; or, for a former prisoner of war, was rated totally disabled for the former-prisoner-of-war total-disability period before death.

Any one of these descriptions is enough for the death condition. Branch (c) concerns a rating of total disability over a stated period; it does not require that the death itself be service-connected.

## 2. The marriage

The spouse must have married the veteran within the post-service marriage period after the period of service, or been married the minimum marriage length or more, or had a child with the veteran.

### Marriage condition — truth table

| Married within the post-service marriage period after the period of service | Married the minimum marriage length or more | Had a child with the veteran | Marriage condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | any | any | Met |
| any | Yes | any | Met |
| any | any | Yes | Met |
| No | No | No | Not met |

The three marriage routes are alternatives: one is enough, and a spouse who meets none of them does not meet the marriage condition.

## Positive and negative cases (hypothetical)

- **Death, branch (c).** A veteran whose death was not service-connected had been rated totally disabled for the whole of the total-disability period before death. The death condition is met.
- **Death, former prisoner of war.** A veteran who was a former prisoner of war had been rated totally disabled for the former-prisoner-of-war total-disability period before death. The death condition is met.
- **Marriage, length on the boundary.** A spouse married to the veteran for exactly the minimum marriage length at the death has been married that length "or more", so the marriage condition is met.
- **Marriage, short with a child.** A spouse married for less than the minimum marriage length, not within the post-service marriage period, who had a child with the veteran, meets the marriage condition through the child.
- **Marriage, none met.** A spouse married for less than the minimum marriage length, outside the post-service marriage period, with no child with the veteran, does not meet the marriage condition.
